head: 87a5f4c
summary: The backing-ribbon fix (87a5f4c) does what it claims, and I found no regression. q12 joint box (x 95-145, y 150-470, median L104): 17 rows had a pixel above median+25 in base, against 0 in head and 0 in the DPR-2 head (box doubled, median L105). At +20 the counts are 24 / 0 / 0, at +15 35 / 0 / 0 and at +10 35 / 0 / 0. The joint still reads as a joint. Its dark groove is unchanged at every sampled row: min L70-62 against a panel median of L107-95 (-37 L) at the same x in base, head and DPR-2 head, as a continuous thin dark line. Panel joints in the official photos (y_47301, py_37301) are thin, faint seams at viewing distance. A crisp groove in a 0.5 m close-up such as q12 is plausible and is no worse than before. Across the 5 views, every base-vs-head difference above 4 L lies inside window panes (animated clouds), except for isolated single pixels. Those were bright sky specks in base along other cell edges and now equal their neighbourhood: q07 x 752-756 and x 22/927 (e.g. 205/211/217 -> 197/199/204, neighbourhood 197/199/204); q14 x 568-570, y 283-326 (200/203/209 -> 184/187/194, neighbourhood equal); q16 (379,201) and (258,223); q03 (278,371). So the fix also cleaned latent specks outside q12. The only odd pixel is q07 (752,163), now 18 L darker than its neighbourhood: one pixel, invisible. No surface is missing or doubled and no new line appears. The mean signed change is about 0 in every view outside the clouds. Nothing is above low. I add +0.1 over confirm2 for the removed speck artefact. The carried low items keep the shell below 9.
